standard.title: Rehearse and present planned performances
standard.description: rehearse and present planned performances in a range of physical and/or virtual spaces
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can perform in a range of forms in informal and formal settings, use peer feedback systematically, and perform via digital platforms (AC9AMU8P01 — Y7-8). They can adapt performance decisions to context. The Y9-10 step adds: performing in a range of physical and virtual spaces as a distinct requirement, recording and evaluating systematically, and performing own compositions with accompanying scores or visual material.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students rehearse and present planned performances in a range of physical and/or virtual spaces, recording and evaluating performances using digital tools, and reflecting on personal and audience responses.

nodes.label: Planning performances for specific spaces
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and adapt performances for specific physical and virtual spaces — making decisions about staging, presentation format and audience interaction suited to each context.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a performance for at least one specific space (physical or virtual); identify at least two decisions that are specific to that space.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and present performances in multiple physical and/or virtual spaces — making context-specific decisions about staging, introduction format, audience interaction, audio/visual requirements; compare how performing in different spaces (classroom, concert hall, assembly, online platform) changes the performance decisions.
wider: Present the same performance in both a physical and a virtual space — compare how the audience interaction, staging and performance decisions differ between the two contexts
Research the specific technical requirements of a venue or platform before performing — use the research to inform preparation decisions

response_modes.reason: Physical and virtual performance contexts each impose genuinely different demands. Students who have only ever performed in one context default to its conventions when placed in another. Each new performance context encountered builds a more flexible and adaptive approach to performance planning.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Virtual performance contexts (streaming, recorded upload, interactive platforms) are increasingly relevant to real-world musical participation — developing fluency in these contexts alongside physical performance is a genuine curricular priority at Y9-10.
success_criteria: Can identify at least two performance decisions that are specific to the space or platform chosen
Adapts at least one aspect of the performance (staging, introduction, or format) in response to the specific context

nodes.label: Recording, evaluating and improving across performances
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can record multiple performances, evaluate them systematically using digital tools, and identify specific improvements made between performances.
nodes.minimum_width: Record at least two performances of the same piece at different stages; compare them and identify at least one specific improvement and one remaining area for development.
nodes.typical_width: Use digital tools to record and systematically evaluate multiple performances — comparing before/after recordings; identifying specific improvements in technique, expression, intonation and stylistic accuracy; documenting what drove improvements; reflecting on personal responses to the performances.
wider: Build a performance portfolio of recordings with written evaluations for each — trace the arc of development across the portfolio and identify the most significant improvements
Evaluate multiple performances from the perspective of both performer and audience — describe how each perspective reveals different aspects of the performance
nodes.hinge_reason: Systematic self-evaluation using recordings — identifying specific changes between performances rather than vague impressions — is the metacognitive practice that drives independent musical improvement. Students who cannot evaluate their own recordings specifically remain dependent on teacher diagnosis. This is the primary skill that distinguishes students who continue to improve without regular teacher instruction from those who plateau.

response_modes.reason: Build a structured recording evaluation protocol: listen once for overall impression, once for technique, once for expression, once for stylistic accuracy. After each focused listen, document one specific observation. The structure prevents students from listening generally and concluding 'it was good/bad' without specific evidence.

success_criteria: Compares at least two recordings of the same piece and identifies at least one specific improvement and one remaining area for development
Can explain what drove the improvement (what they practised or changed)

nodes.label: Performing own compositions with contextual material
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform their own compositions and reflect on personal and audience responses — presenting scores, programme notes or visual material that support audience understanding.
nodes.minimum_width: Present a performance of an original composition with at least brief contextual information (a title, a description of the piece's intention, or a programme note); reflect on one aspect of the audience's or their own response.
nodes.typical_width: Perform original compositions with accompanying scores or visual material; provide programme notes that explain the compositional intention and choices; present in both physical and virtual contexts where possible; compare personal response to the performance with observed audience response; use reflection to inform future compositions.
wider: Present a themed performance program of original works — provide programme notes for each piece and evaluate how well the program communicated its intended theme or message
Compare an original composition performance with a performance of repertoire by another composer — reflect on how the experience of performing your own work differs and what you learn from each

response_modes.reason: Performing original compositions integrates composition, performance, interpretation and reflection into a complete artistic act. The teaching investment is in supporting students to see the performance of their own work as a complete feedback loop: the audience response (or their own listening) generates information that feeds the next compositional decision.

success_criteria: Performs an original composition with contextual information for the audience
Reflects on at least one aspect of personal or audience response and connects it to a future compositional or performance decision
